text: Write the eight-neighbour traversal pattern, skipping the centre and staying inside the grid. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: if (___) continue;          // skip the cell itself
if (___) sum += g[nr][nc];  // stay inside the grid
answer: dr == 0 && dc == 0|r + dr|nr >= 0 && nr < g.length && nc >= 0 && nc < g[nr].length
explanation: Verified: 40, which is 45 minus the centre 5. The offset pair plus a `continue` plus a bounds test is the idiom for this, and it is worth recognising on sight because it appears in every grid problem — cellular automata, image filters, board games, flood fill. Writing the bounds test against `g[nr].length` rather than `g[0].length` is what makes it survive a ragged grid.
